title: Generated text is not authoritative evidence
principal_claim: This talk evaluates a governed workflow that keeps machine candidates, automated checks, human validation and source evidence visibly separate — not a deployed decision engine.
caveat: Not live, not deployed, not automatically authoritative.

title: Inquiry transcripts hide decisions in long, mixed discourse
principal_claim: Public inquiry text holds decision evidence that is lengthy, dispersed and easy to mis-extract as if authoritative.
caveat: Module 2 is a case study, not the sole purpose.

title: Aim: traceable candidates under human oversight
principal_claim: To design and evaluate an LLM-assisted method for creating traceable candidate decision-journal entries from complex public records, using UK COVID-19 Inquiry Module 2 transcripts
caveat: Do not rewrite the aim into a stronger claim.

title: Generation, checks, human review and source stay separate
principal_claim: Later stages do not retrospectively turn machine-generated text into authoritative evidence.
caveat: Research prototype — not production deployment.

title: Evaluation is layered, not a single accuracy number
principal_claim: Bounded lenses answer different questions — none alone is “system accuracy”.
caveat: Do not report a single overall accuracy.

title: Traceable candidates are common; journal-ready ones are not
principal_claim: Pass rates ≠ acceptance. no × high and moderate κ matter more than volume.
caveat: Candidates are not accepted decisions.

title: Quote support ≠ journal membership (phase1-082)
principal_claim: Quotation support does not by itself establish decision-journal validity.
caveat: Extraction tracked the wording; human criterion rejected journal membership.

title: Alignment, faithfulness failure and interpretive mapping
principal_claim: Three verified contrasts; detail remains in the offline demo if requested.
caveat: Framework mapping is not a judgement that performance was good.

title: Contribution is governance of the AI–source–human route
principal_claim: Not a new SOTA extraction algorithm — a governed review process.
caveat: Does not claim deployment readiness.

title: Claims stay bounded to one case, one model, one reviewer
principal_claim: Feasibility evidence, not general policy truth or deployment readiness.
caveat: Do not convert limits into soft claims of strength.

title: Next steps are replication and multi-reviewer checks
principal_claim: Extend evaluation governance — not “add a chatbot and deploy”.
caveat: Not a deployment commitment.

title: Make the route from source to interpretation inspectable
principal_claim: The system does not replace authoritative inquiry evidence or human policy judgement. It makes the route from source evidence to machine-generated candidate and human interpretatio
caveat: Presentation is complete without the live demo.
